title: Octave Boye, Billy Marrero and her husband as band manager
summary: Her husband sent family and others on jobs, learned managing from Billy Marrero, signed contracts and played for a Greenville, Mississippi, man.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Octave Boye. Well, he played for a couple of years, you know. He didn't keep it up. But most of the way he went to play, your daddy would recommend him to go... You know, when people would ask. Well, the most of the way he went through his life playing music, and everybody addressed him always as the past. You know, your daddy would send him, they knew he was the brother, and he'd never take it and explain him. Just Uncle Rudolph would after. Good many years, well, he'd put out his name, Boye, you see. But most of the way your daddy sent him in jobs. Oh, you just get so many jobs, you know. And sometimes he'd split the band, and of course, if he had to take somebody else that maybe wasn't a professional, well, he'd take some of the good men and put them with the man that was a professional. That's how he split the band, you know. Just after a number of years, well, after the union, you know, they didn't go for all that. But he really could master that band. He learned to be a manager under Jimmy Moreira. Jimmy. Billy was the old man. And Simon's dad.

Yeah, Billy Moreira. Billy, that's right. And there's Eddie and Lawrence and Simon. Billy learned him to be a manager. Billy learned him. Because often, I would have had some of them contracts to show you, because I used to still keep them, still keep them. Well, it really got away after. Instead of cheering, my oldest girl, she'd just get along some things, and she'd say, Mama, what do you want this? This is junk. I had contracts that I used to sign. Say, for instance, they play a ball for Carnival tonight. Well, they'd sign that ball for next Carnival right away. The fellow who didn't get them that night said, I'll be at your house in such a time. You know, for deposit. And he always kept a big roll of money home, deposit. You know. And he played a lot for a fellow over in Greenville, Mississippi. I've forgotten that man's name. That man used to come here all the time and hire him. Take him and that man there, Santiago. And about, did you ever know about little Boynell Santiago? Yeah, he was right on it. Yeah, when he played, best of the time, he played with Arnold too, you know, Boynell did. There was another one of those gift-comer fellows, you know. He had another little brother that he died. I forgot what was his name.
